quote: Each party is free to enter into similar agreements with others.

The related dispute mechanics (§ 14.4 mutual jury-trial waiver and § 14.14 two-year actions period) are mutual and do not affect the governing-law analysis. ops.text: 9.3 Excluded Claims. Notwithstanding Sections 9.1 and 9.2 (including Subsection 9.1(c)(2)), the limitations and exclusions of liability in this Section 9 do not apply to Excluded Claims, and each party remains fully liable for its Excluded Claims. "Excluded Claims" means a party's indemnification obligations under Section 8, a party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, a party's gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and a party's infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights. Customer's payment obligations under this Agreement are not damages for purposes of the limitations in this Section 9.

rationale: Sections 9.1 and 9.2 impose substantively identical caps on IBM and on Customer (greater of $100,000 or 12 months' charges paid), and Section 10 contains a mutual consequential-damages exclusion, so mutuality, the fee basis and the damages exclusion meet the playbook (the $100,000 floor rather than USD 1,000,000, and "paid" rather than "paid or payable", are minor shortfalls of the preferred position only). The clause nevertheless fails the fallback on carve-outs: only indemnification payments (9.1(a)/9.2(a)) and bodily-injury/tangible property damage sit outside the cap, with no carve-out for breach of confidentiality, gross negligence or willful misconduct — and Section 6 expressly makes Sections 5, 9 and 10 prevail over the AECI for confidential information in the hosting environment, while 9.1(c)(2) excludes all liability for loss of or damage to Customer's records or data. We therefore added a single mutual Excluded Claims sentence placing confidentiality/data protection and security breaches, indemnities, gross negligence, willful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement outside the Section 9 limits.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We added an express warranty that the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner for 30 days following performance, and that software and Materials deliverables will conform to their documentation for 90 days, with repair, replacement or refund as the remedy. Section 5.1 currently gives no conformance warranty, period or remedy; this is our fallback position and we can work with it.

ops.text: IBM further warrants that (i) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner, and (ii) for 90 days following delivery, any software and Materials deliverable provided under this Agreement will conform to its applicable documentation. The warranty in clause (i) applies for 30 days following performance of the applicable Services. Customer's remedy for breach of these warranties is repair, replacement, or a refund of the charges paid for the non-conforming Services or software.

proposal.summary: Insert a professional and workmanlike Services warranty (30 days from performance) and a 90-day software/deliverable documentation-conformance warranty with repair, replacement or refund remedies.

quote: a. it will perform the Services using reasonable care and skill and in accordance with the applicable Service Option Attachments (which means the degree of knowledge, skill and judgment customarily exercised by members of the applicable profession with respect to work of a similar nature)
rationale: Section 5.1 gives a services standard-of-care warranty (substantively equivalent to "professional and workmanlike") plus a compliance-with-laws covenant, but there is no conformance warranty for any delivered Materials or Base Components, no warranty period, and no remedy for breach. Section 5.4(c) affirmatively provides all Materials "AS IS" and 5.2 makes 5.1 exclusive, so the disclaimer swallows any conformance protection — walk-away territory on the deliverables side and short of the fallback (90 days software / 30 days services with repair, replace, re-perform or refund). Redline adds a 90-day conformance and no-malicious-code warranty with the standard remedy and carves the express warranties out of the "AS IS" disclaimer; the malicious-code element and 12-month software period are noted but we have pitched the 90-day fallback given this is a hosting/services deal.

verification.notes: The single insertion completes every atomic fallback element: professional and workmanlike Services standard, software conformance to documentation, 90-day software period, 30-day Services period measured from performance, and the repair/replacement/refund remedy set. Preferred is not met (90 days rather than 12 months for software, 30 rather than 90 days for services, and no malicious-code warranty), which is expected given the locked fallback target. Minimal: Section 5.1 contained no conformance warranty, period or remedy, so a concise added sentence block is the least intrusive fix; no other sentence was rewritten and no re-performance-only remedy was introduced. Minor tension worth noting (not a deviation): the insertion covers "Materials" deliverables while paragraph (c) provides "ALL MATERIALS ... 'AS IS', WITHOUT WARRANTY OF ANY KIND"; the express Section 5.1 warranty should control as the more specific and later-added term, but a carve-out in (c) would remove any argument. Existing compliance-with-laws covenant is narrower than the playbook preference (limited to laws applicable to IBM's business); note in rationale only.
